subject: Control/Data carveout — on-prem VPC attachment and evidence log
messages:
From: Alex Tilley <alex.tilley@hemera-sys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Singh <nora.singh@hemera-sys.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hemera on‑prem: request for a tight control/data carveout and evidence pack

Karthik, Soojin —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Hemera's security team has a hard requirement: the control plane components for our private deployment must be logically separated from the inference data plane (no shared interfaces except the defined RPC gateway), and we need a small evidence pack for our auditors that proves the separation and egress controls.

Concrete asks from Hemera security:
- A reference diagram showing control plane hosts, management network, and data plane nodes with port-level demarc (TCP/UDP)
- Canary plan for a staged cutover (traffic-slice, verification checks, rollback criteria)
- Egress proof: sample proxy config and where telemetry will be emitted (logs/metrics retention)
- A short list of expected artifact names / timestamps for their audit (e.g., diagram v1, canary run id)

We're targeting a compliance review the week of Jan 11. Can you confirm whether Redwood can deliver the diagram + canary playbook + sample egress config in time? If helpful we can ship a minimal environment for the first canary.

Appreciate a pragmatic path — Hemera would prefer minimal network ACLs at the fabric layer and the heavy lifting in the service boundary.

— Alex
Alex Tilley
Head of Platform Operations — Hemera Systems
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tilley <alex.tilley@hemera-sys.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 13:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hemera on‑prem: request for a tight control/data carveout and evidence pack

Alex —

Thanks — we can do this and align with the Jan 11 compliance window. Summary of proposed deliverables and timeline: 

1) Reference diagram (PDF) — control plane hosts, management VLAN, data plane clusters, RPC gateway, and port-level demarc.
   - Owner: Karthik Iyer (Architecture)
   - Draft: 2026-12-30 EOD (carveout-diagram-v1.pdf)

2) Canary playbook (Markdown) — test plan, traffic-slices (10/30/60), verification checks (latency, error rate, kvcache hit sanity), automated rollback triggers.
   - Owner: Soojin Lee (Ops)
   - Draft: 2026-12-31 noon PST (canary-playbook-v2.md)

3) Egress proof sample — inline proxy snippet + telemetry endpoints + retention notes (text).
   - Owner: Redwood security/ops (I'll attach a config sample)
   - Draft: 2026-12-30 morning (egress-proxy-config-sample.txt)

4) Evidence index — a short CSV/manifest listing artifact names, checksums, and timestamps we will push to your Drive folder.
   - Owner: Karthik, deliver with final email

Notes / technical constraints:
- We will recommend keeping the control plane on a management VLAN that is only routable to the admin bastion + telemetry aggregator. Data plane will run in tenant VLANs with a single NATed egress through the inline proxy.
- For Hemera's minimal ACL preference, we propose strict service-level gating at the RPC gateway (mTLS + JWT validation) rather than broad fabric ACLs. That lets us keep the physical overlay simple while maintaining cryptographic separation.
- Canary plan will include a single tenant-slice run in your staging colo first, then a 3-step roll to preprod. We'll include automated instrumentation and a short checklist of logs/metrics to snapshot for audit.

Attached: carveout-diagram-v1.pdf (diagram stub), egress-proxy-config-sample.txt (example), NOTE: canary playbook still in progress.

If the timeline is good I'll push the artifacts to the shared Drive link and send the evidence index on 12/30.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tilley <alex.tilley@hemera-sys.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Singh <nora.singh@hemera-sys.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hemera on‑prem: request for a tight control/data carveout and evidence pack

Alex / Karthik —

Quick operational addendum from my side:

- Canary sequencing: we will run three verification probes during the slice: token-based smoke, KV cache checksum (sample), and end-to-end latency histogram (p95 target). Each probe will be tied to a Jenkins run that emits a run id and artifact tarball.
- Rollback criteria (examples): 1) p95 latency increase > 35%, 2) error rate > 1.5% over 3 minutes, 3) KV cache miss rate spike > 12%. If any trigger fires we revert the slice and retain the run artifacts for the audit.
- Telemetry: we will forward traces + aggregated metrics to your telemetry collector; logs will be SHA256-indexed and stored for 90 days by default (can expand to 365 on request).

I'll finish the canary-playbook-v2.md by 12/31 and add the Jenkins job name and run templates. Karthik — please confirm whether Hemera wants the management VLAN to have an offsite bastion (yes/no) in the diagram or if the bastion will be hosted inside the customer colo.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Sr. Production Ops Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tilley <alex.tilley@hemera-sys.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Singh <nora.singh@hemera-sys.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Control/Data carveout — on‑prem VPC attachment and evidence log

Alex / team —

Reviewed the diagram and the config snapshot. Hemera — thank you, the separation looks tight and the proposed evidence artifacts are what our compliance team expects. Two quick asks before we upload the final evidence pack to your Drive: 

1) Please confirm bastion placement (Soojin's question). If you host the bastion in your colo we will note that in the manifest and restrict direct management plane IPs in the diagram.

2) We will produce a short CSV manifest with the following columns: artifact_name, artifact_type, sha256, generated_at_utc, owner_contact. Expect that manifest in our final email on 2026-12-30 18:00 UTC.

Deliverables schedule (final):
- 2026-12-30 18:00 UTC — Drive folder updated with:
   * carveout-diagram-v1.pdf
   * egress-proxy-config-sample.txt
   * canary-playbook-v2.md
   * evidence-manifest-HEM-20261230.csv

If Hemera needs expanded retention or an isolated telemetry egress (syslog tunnel + HSM-backed signing) we can scope that as a paid add-on — happy to loop in our Commercial CS contact if you want pricing.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Deployments — Redwood Inference
thread_summary: Hemera requests a control/data plane separation and an audit evidence pack for an on‑prem VPC attachment. Redwood team (Karthik, Soojin, Marissa) agree delivery: diagram, canary playbook, egress sample and artifact manifest. Timeline targets Dec 30 for draft artifacts and Jan 11 compliance review.
